answer: At dawn each agent must forge its identity by locking a refundable stake and completing a small, publicly verifiable task before it can transact. The stake is bonded to one long-lived key; creating a second identity means posting a second stake and redoing the work, so a fable of cheap fake accounts collapses: a Sybil attacker pays linearly per identity, while honest agents pay once and earn the stake back through verified service. Misbehavior slashes the bond, making fake identities expensive to maintain and cheap to expose.
